summary: One functional issue blocks configured Daytona/E2B backends entirely, and one test assertion is permissive enough to miss incorrect failure modes.

findings.message: Configured remote backends can never reach the intended `UNMEASURED` stub path. After credentials are present, `spawn_remote()` unconditionally calls `assert_no_host_map(..., listing=("V:\\", r"V:\Ai", r"V:\OPENWORK"))`, and `_is_v_volume()` immediately raises `BACKEND_ISOLATION` on those hard-coded values. In practice, adding Daytona/E2B credentials makes every remote spawn fail as an isolation violation before any vendor transport is attempted.

This assertion is too weak: `assert raised in (... ) or raised` passes for any truthy exception name, including unrelated failures. The test therefore does not actually pin the expected refusal kinds for `assert_sandbox_cwd(live / "state", ...)`, which can hide regressions.
